author: Mark Atwood
text: DECISION 2026-05-12 (Mark, interactive): multi-file invocation with both run_on_cert (cached single) AND run_on_certs (batch) entry points. The bead's three-option framing was misleading -- audit of zlint's actual CLI showed only one practical shape is supported. ZLINT CLI REALITY (verified ~/GIT/zlint/v3/cmd/zlint/main.go): (1) supports 'zlint cert1 cert2 cert3...' multi-file invocation; loops over flag.Args() linting each file. (2) supports 'zlint -' or 'zlint' (no args) for stdin BUT only one cert per invocation (io.ReadAll + pem.Decode reads single cert from input). (3) NO multi-cert stdin streaming. (4) No daemon mode. The original 'stdin streaming many certs' option doesn't exist in zlint. 'single-call-with-array' and 'file-per-cert' collapse to the same answer when the array is implemented via multi-file CLI invocation. BRIDGE API SHAPE: run_on_cert(&Certificate) -> Result<Vec<(CheckId, Verdict)>, BridgeError> with per-cert hash cache; run_on_certs(&[&Certificate]) -> Result<Vec<Vec<(CheckId, Verdict)>>, BridgeError> for batch. Both required: run_on_cert serves the ~700-Lint adapter from .jy95.1 (cache prevents 700x subprocess); run_on_certs serves CT log scan / compliance audit workflows per non-negotiable #6. IMPLEMENTATION DEFERRED: temp file location (workspace target/ vs /tmp vs /dev/shm), naming (sequential / UUID / hash), cleanup (RAII / batch-end / OS), cache eviction (bounded LRU / unbounded / caller), failure isolation (batch-fails-on-first-error vs skip-bad-cert-continue) -- all are implementation-time questions for PKIX-jy95.7.
